title: Project Hedgehog dependency-ordered 60-day issue graph
ordering_contract: Nodes are ordered so every dependency appears before its dependent node.

gate_definitions.owner-approval: An external write, publication, or contact requires explicit owner approval.
gate_definitions.hardware-required: Acceptance requires measurements from physical Hedgehog hardware; simulation cannot satisfy it.
gate_definitions.test-account-required: Acceptance requires an authorized synthetic or test account, never a private live account.
gate_definitions.authorized-target-only: Security or fault testing is limited to owned, simulated, or explicitly authorized targets.

nodes.title: Import the dependency-ordered 60-day Hedgehog issue graph
nodes.description: Review this local DAG and create or update the corresponding GitHub issues without changing dependency semantics.
acceptance: Every node is represented by a GitHub issue or an explicitly linked existing issue.
Dependencies and milestone labels match this reviewed graph.
The import receipt records issue URLs and the source graph hash.

nodes.title: Create evidence directory conventions and a machine-readable result schema
nodes.description: Gate checked queue items on valid manifests, artifact hashes, and explicit passing checks.
acceptance: The evidence schema and verifier reject unsupported completion claims.
Unit tests cover cross-platform hashing and queue annotations.

nodes.title: Map llama.cpp and GGML CUDA, RPC, MoE, CPU-offload, and device-limit capabilities
nodes.description: Record current upstream capabilities, version-pinned source references, and the exact Hedgehog gaps before custom runtime work.
acceptance: The inventory cites pinned upstream commits and primary source paths.
Supported capabilities and missing Hedgehog layers are separated explicitly.
Reproduction commands and limitations are recorded.

nodes.title: Map UCX, MPI, RDMA-Core, RoCEv2, and InfiniBand options for P100-era systems
nodes.description: Compare established transport stacks against activation-routing, security, operability, and P100-era platform requirements.
acceptance: The matrix cites primary documentation and pinned versions.
TCP, RoCEv2, InfiniBand, UCX, MPI, and RDMA-Core tradeoffs are compared.
Unverified GPUDirect assumptions are labeled for hardware measurement.

nodes.title: Map KVM, libvirt, OpenNebula, and minimal alternatives for stateless hypervisors
nodes.description: Select the smallest established control-plane components that satisfy diskless rebuild, passthrough, placement, and recovery requirements.
acceptance: The component matrix covers immutable boot, libvirt APIs, placement, fencing, and failure recovery.
Operational complexity and security surfaces are compared.
The recommended baseline identifies rejected alternatives and reasons.

nodes.title: Identify P100 and Pascal limitations in current inference stacks and CUDA versions
nodes.description: Pin compiler, driver, compute-capability, kernel, quantization, and upstream-support constraints before building the CUDA environment.
acceptance: The matrix distinguishes documented support, build-only evidence, and hardware-measured evidence.
CUDA, compiler, and driver versions are pinned with primary references.
Known P100 kernel and quantization gaps have minimal reproducers or explicit test plans.

nodes.title: Identify existing expert-parallel implementations that Hedgehog can adapt
nodes.description: Compare static ownership, routing, batching, backpressure, replication, and recovery semantics in established implementations.
acceptance: Candidate implementations are pinned to source versions and compared against Hedgehog requirements.
Reusable components are distinguished from missing integration layers.
License and upstream-divergence constraints are recorded.

nodes.title: Produce ADR-0001 for the virtualized diskless 100Gb fabric architecture
nodes.description: Record the initial architecture for diskless compute nodes, persistent control/storage, whole-device passthrough, NUMA locality, and 100GbE or EDR fabric.
acceptance: The ADR states context, decision, alternatives, consequences, and measurable assumptions.
Control, storage, management, and inference failure domains are explicit.
Hardware-dependent assumptions are listed as unverified rather than asserted.

nodes.title: Produce Threat Model v0.1 for Hedgehog and SK Companies tenant workloads
nodes.description: Define assets, trust boundaries, threat actors, abuse cases, controls, recovery requirements, and validation plans for the target architecture.
acceptance: Management, storage, inference, development, and experimental trust boundaries are modeled.
Secrets, artifact provenance, egress, tenant isolation, audit, backup, and recovery threats have controls and tests.
Residual risks and owner decisions are explicit.

nodes.title: Establish CI that rejects unsupported completion claims and missing evidence links
nodes.description: Run the existing evidence verifier and full Hedgehog unit suite on relevant repository changes.
acceptance: A repository workflow runs evidence verification and all Hedgehog unit tests.
A deliberately unsupported checked queue item causes a failing CI run.
A clean baseline produces a passing CI run with retained logs.

nodes.title: Build the static expert-ownership simulation
nodes.description: Simulate deterministic model-expert ownership, activation routing, replica selection, load distribution, and worker loss without claiming hardware performance.
acceptance: Fixed seeds produce deterministic expert assignments and routes.
The simulation reports imbalance, replica placement, and dropped or retried work.
Fixtures distinguish simulated capacity from physical measurements.

nodes.title: Define numerical reference tests for distributed MoE execution
nodes.description: Compare routed and aggregated outputs to a single-process reference across deterministic fixtures and tolerances.
acceptance: Reference fixtures cover routing, aggregation, duplicate experts, and empty routes.
Tolerances are justified independently of the implementation under test.
Injected routing or aggregation mutations cause deterministic failures.

nodes.title: Build the activation-routing transport benchmark
nodes.description: Measure synthetic activation payload latency, throughput, batching, compression, and backpressure over locally available transports.
acceptance: Payload distributions are derived from explicit synthetic MoE shapes.
Commands, versions, warmup, repetitions, raw samples, and summary statistics are retained.
Local simulation results are not labeled as 100Gb fabric measurements.

nodes.title: Build a topology fixture parser for NUMA, PCIe, GPUs, NICs, and memory channels
nodes.description: Normalize captured and synthetic topology sources into a deterministic machine-readable hardware graph.
acceptance: Synthetic fixtures cover multiple NUMA roots, missing fields, and malformed data.
The normalized graph preserves source provenance and unknown values.
Placement consumers receive stable identifiers and explicit locality relationships.

nodes.title: Define failure-injection tests for worker, NIC, VM, and expert loss
nodes.description: Create deterministic simulated faults and recovery assertions before hardware-backed fencing and failover tests.
acceptance: Each fault names detection, containment, retry, fencing, and recovery expectations.
Deterministic simulations cover worker, VM, NIC-path, and expert-replica loss.
Recovery time and correctness are recorded separately.

nodes.title: Create a one-command hardware inventory collector
nodes.description: Collect CPU, NUMA, DIMM, PCIe, GPU, NIC, firmware, IOMMU, sensor, and RDMA facts with source provenance.
acceptance: One documented command emits a schema-valid inventory and raw source captures.
Unknown or unavailable values remain explicit instead of inferred.
A second run on the same unchanged host is reproducibly comparable.

nodes.title: Create a reproducible CUDA 12 and Pascal environment
nodes.description: Pin base image, compiler, CUDA toolkit, drivers, libraries, build flags, and provenance for P100-compatible workloads.
acceptance: The environment is generated from pinned inputs with artifact provenance.
Pascal-target builds complete in an available build environment.
Runtime claims remain blocked until P100 execution evidence exists.

nodes.title: Create the PXE and iPXE immutable hypervisor prototype
nodes.description: Build a reproducible stateless boot flow with authenticated artifacts, central configuration, and replacement-node registration.
acceptance: A nested or simulated node boots from pinned artifacts without worker-local unique configuration.
Artifact verification and unauthorized-image rejection are tested.
Rebuild and replacement procedures are reproducible from a clean fixture.

nodes.title: Create VFIO whole-GPU and whole-NIC passthrough automation
nodes.description: Generate topology-aware libvirt device assignments with IOMMU isolation, NUMA pinning, and rollback checks.
acceptance: Synthetic topology tests reject unsafe IOMMU groups and cross-NUMA placement.
Generated definitions are idempotent and reversible.
Physical acceptance proves whole-device assignment and host recovery after VM teardown.

nodes.title: Create one-, two-, and four-P100 acceptance test plans
nodes.description: Define correctness, performance, locality, utilization, thermal, power, and recovery evidence needed at each scale.
acceptance: Each scale has exact commands, models or synthetic fixtures, metrics, repetitions, and pass criteria.
NUMA, PCIe, VRAM, RAM, network, power, and temperature observations are required where applicable.
Plans do not pre-assert hardware results.

nodes.title: Produce the Family Media Digest technical-feasibility and legal-boundary matrix
nodes.description: Classify each proposed data source and feature by authorized access path, coverage, latency, privacy risk, and required review.
acceptance: Every source is classified as supported, partial, metadata-only, export-only, or unavailable.
Consent, account authority, retention, and human-review boundaries are explicit.
No private production data is used as evidence.

nodes.title: Prototype authorized Android collection on synthetic accounts
nodes.description: Evaluate UsageStatsManager and NotificationListenerService collection boundaries with consent, minimization, provenance, and failure handling.
acceptance: Only synthetic or authorized test-account data is collected.
Permission denial, revocation, duplicate events, and offline buffering are tested.
Captured fields and unavailable content are documented exactly.

nodes.title: Verify TikTok export contents and latency using a test account
nodes.description: Measure the authorized export workflow, field coverage, timestamp fidelity, and delivery latency without inferring unavailable conversations.
acceptance: The test-account request and receipt timestamps are retained.
Fields, omissions, and coverage limits are enumerated from the received export.
No private live-account payload is committed.

nodes.title: Verify Meta Family Center supervising-parent data coverage
nodes.description: Distinguish FULL, PARTIAL, and METADATA_ONLY conversation coverage using authorized test accounts and documented surfaces.
acceptance: Coverage classifications are backed by authorized observed fields and timestamps.
Unavailable message content is never inferred from metadata.
Permission and supervision-state changes are tested.

nodes.title: Prototype Life360 and Family Link context ingestion
nodes.description: Use authorized notifications and events, preserve source confidence, and document unavailable official API surfaces.
acceptance: Synthetic event fixtures cover duplicates, gaps, reordering, and permission loss.
Each field records its authorized source and confidence.
Unavailable APIs and prohibited workarounds are documented.

nodes.title: Build a synthetic daily digest pipeline with concern alerts and false-positive scoring
nodes.description: Exercise ingestion, normalization, concern rules or models, evidence attribution, escalation, and human review on synthetic data.
acceptance: Synthetic scenarios include true positives, false positives, missing data, and conflicting sources.
Every alert cites the source events and confidence used.
Precision, recall, false-positive rate, and abstention are reported without production claims.

nodes.title: Measure one-, two-, and four-P100 single-host inference baselines
nodes.description: Run pinned dense and MoE workloads across quantizations, context lengths, CPU affinity, RAM offload, and NUMA placement.
acceptance: Correctness passes against the defined reference before performance claims.
Raw latency, throughput, utilization, memory, locality, power, and temperature data are retained.
Each result identifies exact hardware topology, model, quantization, and software versions.

nodes.title: Measure the 100GbE or EDR InfiniBand fabric baseline
nodes.description: Characterize bandwidth, latency, CPU cost, NUMA locality, reliability, and representative activation payloads across candidate transports.
acceptance: Synthetic and representative activation payload results are both retained.
TCP and the selected RDMA path are measured with NUMA placement documented.
Raw samples, counters, errors, versions, and topology are reproducible.

nodes.title: Build the two-host activation-routing and static-shard prototype
nodes.description: Move activations between stable expert owners while keeping model shards resident, with reference-correct outputs and retained network profiles.
acceptance: Outputs match the numerical reference within justified tolerances.
Steady state moves activations rather than repeatedly transferring expert weights.
Network, PCIe, CPU, GPU, and RAM residency evidence is retained.

nodes.title: Implement multi-host expert routing, batching, and backpressure
nodes.description: Extend the two-host prototype to deterministic multi-host routing with bounded queues, load metrics, and failure-safe request handling.
acceptance: Routing remains reference-correct under batching and controlled overload.
Backpressure bounds memory and reports rejected or delayed work explicitly.
Per-node expert load and end-to-end latency are retained.

nodes.title: Implement expert replication and recovery after worker loss
nodes.description: Place replicas across failure domains, detect unavailable owners, reroute deterministically, and preserve request correctness.
acceptance: Replica placement avoids the modeled single failure domains.
Deliberate worker loss triggers bounded detection and reference-correct rerouting.
Recovery time, retries, duplicate work, and lost requests are measured.

nodes.title: Expose Hedgehog as a NUMA-aware, GPU-seat-aware resource pool
nodes.description: Schedule single-P100, multi-P100, multi-host, batch, and interactive workloads without treating aggregate VRAM as coherent memory.
acceptance: Placement honors GPU seat, IOMMU, NUMA, RAM, NIC, and model-shard constraints.
Worker-local state is replaceable and unhealthy resources are fenced.
Priority, queueing, and safe preemption behavior have deterministic tests.

nodes.title: Run security and fault-containment exercises
nodes.description: Validate segmentation, least privilege, provenance, egress, audit, backup, fencing, and compromise containment on owned or simulated systems.
acceptance: Each exercise maps to a threat-model control and expected containment boundary.
Deliberate node, VM, NIC-path, service, and credential-scope failures are retained as evidence.
Recovery and residual-risk results are independently reviewed.

nodes.title: Build the integrated observability and benchmark suite
nodes.description: Collect correctness, latency, throughput, utilization, locality, traffic, power, temperature, errors, recovery, and cost metrics with reproducible metadata.
acceptance: Raw samples and environment manifests accompany every summary.
Tokens per second, time to first token, prompt rate, component utilization, traffic, power, temperature, errors, and recovery are captured where applicable.
Cost per million useful tokens includes documented assumptions and sensitivity.

nodes.title: Validate four-host scale, expert replication, and power-aware scheduling
nodes.description: Measure multi-host scaling and recovery under representative workloads while exercising capacity-aware power control.
acceptance: Correctness remains within reference tolerances at four-host scale.
Scaling, imbalance, saturation, power, and thermal behavior are measured from raw data.
Deliberate loss of workers, VMs, and NIC paths produces bounded, measured recovery.

nodes.title: Produce the integrated Hedgehog release candidate and 60-day evidence package
nodes.description: Assemble the reproducible build, benchmark suite, security review, architecture, failure-mode, cost, power, and roadmap artifacts for owner acceptance.
acceptance: A competent operator can reproduce the build and documented workloads without undocumented rituals.
Security, correctness, performance, recovery, cost, and power claims link to validated raw evidence.
Unavailable model weights or unmet hardware targets remain explicit roadmap gaps.
Owner acceptance records scope, rollback or recovery evidence, and residual risks.
